HediffDef.label: head cold
HediffDef.description: A common cold: a virus caught from someone who has it. A runny nose, sneezing and a sore throat for about a week, worst around the second or third day. Nothing cures it, but rest in bed, warmth and plenty to drink help the body throw it off sooner, and tending eases it a little. It can leave a cough behind for a few days. In the old, the frail and the starving, a cold can turn into pneumonia.

notes.li: Rest, warmth and plenty to drink. It runs its course in about a week whatever we do; the ones who stay in bed get over it sooner.
[lowtech] Hot broth, a warm bed and a cup of honey water at night. A cold goes when it's ready. Keep the old ones warm.
[!lowtech] No medicine cures a cold. Fluids, rest and something for the aches. Keep an eye on the old and the frail: that's where a cold turns into pneumonia.

HediffDef.label: stomach bug
HediffDef.description: A stomach virus that passes from hand to mouth and goes through a household in days. A day or two of cramps, vomiting and running to the latrine, then a day of feeling weak. Unlike food poisoning it isn't the meal that's to blame but whoever had it last: the cook, a shared cup, the door handle. Rest and plenty to drink are what help; the danger is drying out. Washing hands before cooking stops it going round.

notes.li: Water, a little at a time, and a bowl by the bed. It's over in two days for most. Wash hands before cooking, or it goes round again.
[lowtech] Boiled water with a pinch of salt, and keep the sick ones out of the kitchen. Two days, and they'll be eating again.
[!lowtech] Fluids with salt and sugar so they don't dry out. Disinfect the latrine and keep the sick out of the kitchen until a day after it stops.

HediffDef.label: chest cold
HediffDef.description: An infection of the airways (bronchitis), often after a cold: a deep, chesty cough that lasts a week or two, with tiredness and a tight chest. It's worse for those who stay out in the cold. Warmth, rest and plenty to drink help; tending eases the cough, but no medicine cures it. In the old, the frail and the starving it can turn into pneumonia.

notes.li: Keep them warm and out of the wind. The cough will hang on for a couple of weeks, and that's normal. If they get feverish and short of breath, call me at once: that's pneumonia.
[lowtech] Steam from a pot of hot water, honey for the throat, and a warm bed. Watch the old ones.
[!lowtech] It's viral, so antibiotics won't touch it. Warmth, fluids, rest. Watch for a high fever or labored breathing.

HediffDef.label: hay fever
HediffDef.description: An allergy to pollen: sneezing, a streaming nose and itchy, watering eyes while the plants are in flower. It isn't catching, but it wears on people. It settles much faster indoors, away from the pollen. Tending soothes it, and modern medicine (an antihistamine) works best. The same people tend to suffer from it every year.

notes.li: Keep them indoors on windy days and wash the pollen off their face and hands in the evening. It lasts as long as the flowers do.
[lowtech] Nettle and chamomile tea, a wet cloth over the eyes, and indoor work for a few days.
[!lowtech] An antihistamine from the medicine shelf works well. Indoor work for a few days helps more than anything.

HediffDef.label: pinkeye
HediffDef.description: Conjunctivitis: an infection of the thin skin over the eye, passed on by hands and shared cloths. Red, itchy, weeping eyes for about a week; it blurs the sight but does no lasting harm. Clean hands and separate towels stop it spreading. Tending soothes it, and modern eye drops clear it much faster.

notes.li: Wash the eyes with clean water, and nobody shares a towel. It's gone in a week.
[lowtech] Bathe the eyes in cooled boiled water morning and night, and keep their hands away from their faces.
[!lowtech] Antibiotic drops if it's bacterial, which shortens it a lot. Separate towels and pillowcases until it's gone.

HediffDef.label: dreamfever
HediffDef.description: A rim fever with no known cause that spreads among people who sleep near each other. It brings a mild fever and dreams so vivid they spill over into the waking day: the sick are confused, slow and restless at night. Most shake it off in five or six days. Rest, quiet and cool cloths help; no medicine does much.

notes.li: Cool cloths, a quiet room and someone to sit with them when they wake. Don't argue with what they saw. It passes in a few days.
[lowtech] The old wives say a sprig of lavender under the pillow helps. It can't hurt.
[!lowtech] The scanner shows nothing wrong but a mild fever and a very busy brain. Rest and fluids.

HediffDef.label: strained back
HediffDef.description: A strained muscle in the lower back from too many heavy loads: pain, stiffness and trouble bending. A day or two of rest in bed helps most at the start, then light work; it eases within one to two weeks. Tending (strapping, a warm compress) speeds it along. It comes from long days of hauling, mining and building, more often in older backs.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has strained {PAWN_possessive} back with all the heavy work.

notes.li: A day or two in bed, then light work until it stops twinging. Lift with the legs.
[lowtech] Warm stones wrapped in cloth on the sore spot, and nothing heavier than a bucket for a week.
[!lowtech] Heat, rest, then gentle movement, and painkillers if they need them. It'll mend in a week or two.

HediffDef.label: sore hands
HediffDef.description: Aching, swollen tendons in the hands and wrists from long days of the same fine work at a bench. It clears in about a week if the hands get a rest; tending (a splint, a cold compress) helps.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef}'s hands are sore from long hours at the bench.

notes.li: Rest the hands. Other work for a few days, nothing that grips.
[lowtech] Cold well water on the wrists, a cloth splint at night, and no fine work for a week.
[!lowtech] A wrist brace at night and something for the swelling. Put them on other work for a few days.

HediffDef.label: blisters
HediffDef.description: Raw blisters on the feet from a long day's walking or a caravan on the move. Sore for a few days; kept clean and dry, they heal without trouble. Tending (cleaning and dressing them) helps them heal faster.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has blisters from all the walking.

notes.li: Clean them, cover them, and don't pop them. Dry feet at night.
[lowtech] Wash the feet, wrap them in clean linen, and let them air by the fire at night.
[!lowtech] Clean, a blister dressing, and dry socks. They'll be fine in a few days.

HediffDef.label: chilblains
HediffDef.description: Itchy, swollen red patches on the fingers and toes after hours of work in cold, damp air, as small blood vessels react to the cold. It isn't frostbite and does no lasting harm. Warmed slowly and kept dry, it clears in a week or so. Warm clothes and indoor work on the coldest days prevent it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has chilblains from working out in the cold.

notes.li: Warm them up slowly, not right by the fire. Dry gloves and indoor work for a while.
[lowtech] Wool, more wool, and no scratching. A little goose fat on the cracked skin.
[!lowtech] Gradual rewarming and a soothing lotion for the itch. Better gloves next time.

HediffDef.label: sunburn
HediffDef.description: Skin burned by hours under a hot midday sun with nothing on the head. Red, hot and painful for a day or two, then it peels; it heals in under a week. Cool water, shade and a soothing salve help. A hat prevents it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} is sunburned from working bareheaded in the heat.

notes.li: Cool water, shade and plenty to drink. A hat next time.
[lowtech] Aloe if we have it, cool wet cloths if we don't. And a wide-brimmed hat.
[!lowtech] Cool compresses and aloe gel. Keep them out of the sun until it stops stinging.

HediffDef.label: smoke cough
HediffDef.description: A dry, scratchy cough from hours in a small room with a wood fire burning and nowhere for the smoke to go. A day or two of clean air clears it. A bigger room, or the fire somewhere else, prevents it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a cough from the smoke in that small room.

notes.li: Fresh air. That's all it needs, and a room where the smoke can get out.
[lowtech] Move the fire to a bigger room, or open a smoke hole in the roof.
[!lowtech] Get them out of the smoke. Better yet, swap that fire for a proper heater.

HediffDef.label: toothache
HediffDef.description: A rotten tooth: a dull ache that turns into a throb whenever they chew or drink something cold. Sweets and the years make it likelier. It comes and goes on its own for a couple of weeks, but one good treatment deals with it: the tooth is cleaned and filled, or pulled.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a toothache.

notes.li: That tooth needs seeing to. One treatment should settle it.
[lowtech] Clove oil on the gum for the pain, then the pliers. It's quick.
[!lowtech] Clean it out and fill it. And go easy on the sweets.

HediffDef.label: stiff neck
HediffDef.description: A crick in the neck from a night on the ground, a bedroll or a hard bed. A day or two of stiffness that eases with warmth and gentle movement; no doctor needed. A proper bed prevents it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} woke up with a stiff neck.

notes.li: A warm cloth and some gentle stretching. A real bed would help more than I can.
[lowtech] Warm stones in a cloth on the neck. A mattress of fresh straw would stop it happening.
[!lowtech] Heat and a gentle massage. A proper mattress would stop it happening.

HediffDef.label: sprained ankle
HediffDef.description: A twisted ankle from a bad step on rough, wet or snowy ground: the ligaments are stretched and the joint swells. Rest, cold, strapping and keeping the foot up help; it heals in a week or so, faster with time in bed at the start.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has sprained an ankle on the rough ground.

notes.li: Rest, cold, strapping, and the foot up. A day or two in bed, then a stick to lean on.
[lowtech] Cold water from the stream, a tight linen wrap and a crutch.
[!lowtech] Ice, a compression bandage and the foot raised. Painkillers for the first days.

HediffDef.label: eye strain
HediffDef.description: Tired, aching eyes and a headache from hours of close work in poor light. A good night's sleep clears it. Better light where they work prevents it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a headache from working in poor light.

notes.li: Sleep is the cure. A lamp at that workbench is the prevention.
[lowtech] A torch or a candle by the bench, and rest the eyes now and then.
[!lowtech] A lamp at the bench, and look up from the work every so often.

HediffDef.label: rimrot cough
HediffDef.description: A wet, rattling cough from sleeping in a damp, moldy room: a dirty room under solid rock, one open to the rain, or anywhere grimy in a swamp or jungle. The mold settles in the chest and lingers for a week or so. A clean, dry, well-roofed bedroom is the cure, and tending eases it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a rimrot cough from sleeping in a damp room.

notes.li: Clean that room and fix the roof, or the cough will just come back.
[lowtech] Dry the room out with a fire, sweep it, and air the bedding in the sun.
[!lowtech] Scrub the mold off, patch the roof, and run a heater to dry the place out.

HediffDef.label: ash lung
HediffDef.description: A dry cough and a tight chest from breathing ash and soot: from beating out fires, or from working under volcanic ashfall. Gray phlegm for a few days, then it clears in clean air. Rest and tending help.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a chestful of ash and soot.

notes.li: Clean air and rest. A wet cloth over the mouth next time.
[lowtech] Steam and honey for the throat, and a wet rag over the face when fighting fires.
[!lowtech] Rest and fluids; it'll clear. Masks for whoever fights the next fire.

HediffDef.label: insomnia
HediffDef.description: Nights of lying awake, from worry or from being up in the small hours too often. They fall asleep late, wake early and get less out of the sleep they do have, and the tiredness builds through the day. A regular bedtime, no work after dark, something warm to drink and a quiet room help, and a doctor can give them something to help them sleep for a few nights. It passes in a week or so once whatever keeps them up eases. Night owls don't get it from late hours.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} hasn't been sleeping properly.

notes.li: The same bedtime every night, and no work once it's dark. Something warm to drink before bed.
[lowtech] Chamomile, or warm milk with honey, before bed. Nothing heavier than mending after dark, and no talk of raids at supper.
[!lowtech] A dark room and a fixed bedtime. Something mild from the medicine shelf for a few nights, no longer than that.

HediffDef.label: migraine
HediffDef.description: A pounding headache, usually on one side, with sickness and eyes that can't bear the light. It tends to come after missed meals, worry or a bad night, and lasts most of a day. Lying down in a dark, quiet room helps most, and twice as fast as working through it. A doctor can ease the pain, and modern painkillers work best.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a migraine and needs a dark room.

notes.li: Bed, curtains drawn, and quiet. A cold cloth on the forehead. It'll be gone by morning.
[lowtech] Willow bark tea, a cold cloth and a dark corner. Make sure they eat something once they can.
[!lowtech] Painkillers early, before it takes hold, then a dark room. Regular meals keep them away.

HediffDef.label: heartburn
HediffDef.description: A burning ache behind the breastbone after a rich, heavy meal, worse when lying down. Common and harmless; it's over in a few hours. Smaller helpings, sitting up for a while after eating and not eating late prevent it. It gets more common from middle age on.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has heartburn after that rich meal.

notes.li: Sit up, sip some water and wait. Smaller helpings next time.
[lowtech] A cup of milk or a pinch of chalk in water. And don't lie down straight after a feast.
[!lowtech] Something from the shelf to settle the stomach, if it's bad. Mostly, smaller helpings.

HediffDef.label: nosebleed
HediffDef.description: A nosebleed from freezing air that dries and cracks the inside of the nose. It looks worse than it is: pinched shut with the head tipped forward, it stops within the hour, and the nose is tender for a while after. A scarf over the face in the bitter cold prevents it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a nosebleed from the freezing air.

notes.li: Pinch the soft part of the nose and lean forward, not back. It stops.
[lowtech] A cold stone on the back of the neck and the nose pinched. A scarf over the face next time.
[!lowtech] Pressure for ten minutes, head forward. A little grease inside the nose stops the cracking.

HediffDef.label: motion sickness
HediffDef.description: Queasiness, sweating and the odd bout of sickness from days on the move with a caravan: the sway of the pack animals and a road that never keeps still. It eases once the caravan stops and is gone within a day of arriving. Walking beside the animals instead of riding, fresh air, eyes on the horizon and something plain to eat help; ginger is the old remedy. Children are prone to it, old travelers much less.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} is travel-sick from the caravan's sway.

notes.li: Walk, don't ride, and keep your eyes on the horizon. Dry bread, small sips of water.
[lowtech] Chew a piece of ginger root and walk at the front, where the air is fresh.
[!lowtech] Something for the nausea from the kit, plain food, and the window seat if there is one.

HediffDef.label: splinter
HediffDef.description: A sliver of wood driven deep into the hand from felling and handling trees. Sore and fiddly rather than dangerous: any doctor can pick it out in one go, and left alone it works its way out in a week or so. Gloves prevent it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a splinter deep in one hand.

notes.li: A clean needle, good light and a steady hand. Out it comes.
[lowtech] Soak the hand in warm water, then the needle, heated in the fire first. Gloves for the woodcutters.
[!lowtech] Tweezers, a dab of antiseptic and a plaster. Gloves for anyone felling trees.

HediffDef.label: insect bites
HediffDef.description: Dozens of itchy, swollen bites from the mosquitoes and biting flies of the swamps and jungles. They itch for a few days and keep people up at night. Smoke from a fire, long sleeves, a net over the bed and not scratching help, and a soothing salve takes the edge off.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has been eaten alive by the insects.

notes.li: Don't scratch. Cool water on the bites, and long sleeves out there.
[lowtech] A paste of clay and crushed leaves on the bites, and a smoky fire at dusk to keep them off.
[!lowtech] Anti-itch cream from the shelf. Nets over the beds would save us a lot of this.

HediffDef.label: plant rash
HediffDef.description: An itchy, blistering rash on the hands and arms from the sap of some wild plant, picked up while weeding, harvesting or cutting. It isn't catching. Washing the skin right after the work helps, gloves and long sleeves prevent it, and a soothing salve eases the itch while it heals over a week or so; modern creams work best.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has an itchy rash from some plant's sap.

notes.li: Wash it with plenty of water and keep the hands out of the fields for a few days.
[lowtech] Oatmeal in cool water for the itch, and find out which plant it was before someone else touches it.
[!lowtech] A steroid cream clears it in days. Gloves and long sleeves for the field hands.

HediffDef.label: frostnip
HediffDef.description: The first stage of frostbite, on cheeks, nose and fingertips left bare in bitter cold: the skin goes white and numb, then stings as it warms. Warmed gently, without rubbing, it does no lasting harm and is gone within a day or so. A hood, a scarf and mittens prevent it; harder cold brings real frostbite.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has frostnip on the fingertips and cheeks.

notes.li: Warm it slowly against the skin, never by the fire, and don't rub it. Mittens next time.
[lowtech] Hands under the armpits, a warm drink and a fur hood. Snow rubbed on it is an old mistake.
[!lowtech] Lukewarm water, not hot, and no rubbing. Better gloves for whoever works out there.

HediffDef.label: heat rash
HediffDef.description: Prickly heat: tiny itchy red bumps where sweat is trapped under clothes in hot, sticky weather. Harmless, and gone in a day or two once the skin can breathe. Cool water, loose clothes, shade and a cooler room to sleep in help.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has prickly heat from the sticky weather.

notes.li: Cool water, loose clothes, and the coolest room we have at night.
[lowtech] A cool wash in the evening and a linen shirt instead of wool.
[!lowtech] Calamine for the itch, and a cooler in the bedrooms before the next heat.

HediffDef.label: cold sore
HediffDef.description: A small, painful blister at the edge of the lip, from a virus that sleeps in the skin and wakes with worry, strong sun or a cold. It crusts over and heals in about a week, and passes to others by kissing and shared cups while it weeps. Modern medicine (an antiviral cream) shortens it a good deal.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has a cold sore on {PAWN_possessive} lip.

notes.li: Leave it alone and keep your own cup. A week, and it's gone.
[lowtech] A dab of honey or lemon balm on it, and no kissing anyone for a week.
[!lowtech] Antiviral cream, early. Own cup, own towel until it's crusted over.

HediffDef.label: lice
HediffDef.description: Head and body lice, picked up in a crowded, dirty sleeping room or from someone who has them: constant itching, worse at night. They pass to whoever sleeps in the same dirty room. A fine comb, boiled bedding and clothes, short hair and a clean room get rid of them, and a doctor's treatment clears them in a day or two; left alone they hang on for a couple of weeks. The same body lice carry typhus, so someone with lice in dirty quarters is three times as likely to catch it.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has lice.

notes.li: A fine comb, every evening, and all the bedding boiled. Then scrub that room.
[lowtech] Cut the hair short, boil every blanket and shirt, and comb through with vinegar. The whole room, or they'll be back.
[!lowtech] A delousing wash for everyone in that room, and the bedding through the hottest wash we have.

HediffDef.label: athlete's foot
HediffDef.description: A fungus between the toes from feet that stay wet: itchy, cracked, peeling skin that stings. It comes from days of wading through water, marsh and mud, and clears in a week or two once the feet are kept dry. Dry socks, airing the feet in the evening and drying carefully between the toes help; a doctor's powder, or better a modern antifungal cream, clears it faster.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has athlete's foot from wading through the wet.

notes.li: Dry feet. Dry socks every morning and bare feet in the evening.
[lowtech] Wash and dry between the toes, then a dusting of wood ash. Boots off by the fire at night.
[!lowtech] Antifungal cream twice a day and clean, dry socks. Nobody borrows anyone's boots.

HediffDef.label: hiccups
HediffDef.description: Hiccups after a drink or a big, rich meal: a spasm of the breathing muscle every few seconds that won't stop for a while. Harmless; they stop on their own within an hour or two. Holding the breath, a slow drink of water or a good fright are the old cures.

li.gotText: {PAWN_nameDef} has the hiccups.

notes.li: Hold your breath and count to twenty. Or wait.

HediffDef.label: lingering cough
HediffDef.description: The cough that hangs on after a cold or a chest infection. Annoying rather than harmful; it fades within a week or two.

notes.li: It's just the cough hanging on. It'll go.

HediffDef.label: convalescing
HediffDef.description: Weak and tired after an illness, an operation, a long time in bed or a lost limb, while the body rebuilds its strength. Work and walking are a little slower for a while. Rest, good food and time are all it needs, and time in bed shortens it. Back at work while still weak, it can set itself back a couple of days; a visit from a friend makes the bed easier to bear.

notes.li: Plenty of food and sleep, and light work until the strength comes back.

HediffDef.label: nerve pain
HediffDef.description: A burning, aching pain where the shingles rash was, after the blisters have healed: the nerve underneath is slow to settle. It fades over a week or two. Warmth, rest and something for the pain help.

notes.li: It's the nerve, still sore after the rash. It fades.
